title: Hong Shao Rou
subtitle: Chinese red-braised pork belly
excerpt: The most celebrated pork dish in Chinese home cooking: pork belly simmered for two hours in soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sugar, and spices until the skin turns glossy and mahogany-red and the fat beneath it melts to silk. Associated with Mao Zedong and the food of Hunan.

recipe.sourceNotes: Hong shao rou (红烧肉, red-braised pork) is one of the cornerstones of Chinese home cooking and exists in versions across nearly every regional cuisine. The Shanghainese version is sweeter and uses yellow Shaoxing wine; the Hunanese version (associated with Mao Zedong, who was said to have eaten it regularly) is spiced with star anise and less sweet. The red colour comes from the caramelisation of rock sugar and the deep reduction of the soy sauce. Cooking the pork skin-side down and building up a crust of caramelised glaze is a standard technique that ensures the skin becomes gelatinous rather than tough. The dish improves dramatically if made the day before and reheated.

recipeTools.notes: A casserole or braising pan with a lid.

content.text: Blanch the pork belly first to remove impurities and tighten the skin. The caramelising of the sugar before adding the pork is what produces the mahogany colour: cook the sugar until it is very dark, almost burnt, before adding the wine and soy. Cook on the lowest possible heat for the full 2 hours; hard simmering will toughen the meat.

items.preparation: skin-on, cut into 4 cm cubes or left as a slab

content.text: Blanch the pork in a pan of boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse, and pat dry. Heat the oil in a casserole over medium heat. Add the sugar and cook without stirring until it turns dark amber. Add the Shaoxing wine (it will spit) and stir quickly to dissolve the caramel. Add the soy sauces, ginger, garlic, star anise, and cinnamon stick.
Add the pork pieces and enough water to just cover (about 400 ml). Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 1.5 hours, turning the pork halfway through.

Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium. Cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes, turning the pork frequently, until the liquid has reduced to a thick, glossy sauce that coats the pork. The pork skin should be dark mahogany and the fat underneath completely tender. Serve with steamed rice and scatter with spring onion.
